rationale: The reachable statement executor calls auto_begin before DML and auto_commit afterward. However, auto_begin delegates to begin, which changes the auto_commit flag to false; the later auto_commit therefore skips commit and leaves that transaction active. DDL follows a separate direct-save path, so none of the four options fully describes the mixed behavior.

After the signal, serve times out only the accept-loop task. That loop spawned every connection task without retaining its handle, so it can finish immediately on the shutdown notification while in-flight handlers remain detached; main then returns Ok and the runtime drops them. This is neither the intended bounded drain nor any complete non-gold option.

The live server invokes the parser, whose imports cover sibling HTTP types and the crate error type and whose code uses std::str, with no router dependency. Yet the parser also has no internal helper submodules and does depend outside http through crate::error, so option D is absent as written in addition to option C; the NOT-present prompt has no unique answer.

The crate exports implementations for the six specified middleware categories, but the executable constructs an empty App stack and registers only Logging, RateLimit, Gzip, and Cors. Consequently the alternative set in B is inconsistent, while C's exactly-six default-chain claim and D's default BasicAuth placement are also inconsistent, yielding multiple answers.

Exact-method registration makes option C inconsistent, while HEAD fallback and parameter capture are reachable. But an unregistered OPTIONS request also fails: Router::resolve returns None before dispatch can enter its successful-match branch that creates the Allow response. Thus both B and C are inconsistent with the implementation.

Dispatch reaches a literal/parameter/wildcard trie, but each lookup allocates a segment Vec and repeatedly constructs route Strings; wildcard lookup additionally allocates and leaks a synthetic Node after cloning its handlers. The only-parameter-map allocation guarantee in B is therefore false, while A, C, and D describe different router architectures.

The executable installs this Router and handle_connection calls its trie lookup, but lookup first collects path segments into a Vec, wildcard matching builds another Vec and joined String, and the result clones the route middleware Vec. Hence B's only-parameter-map allocation claim does not hold, and none of the alternative architectural options matches.
